title: ‘अग्रगामी कथा’मा नारीचेतना [Women's consciousness in 'Aragami Katha']
nepali: नारीवादी आन्दोलनको उपलब्धिका रूपमा पाश्चात्य साहित्यशास्त्रमा स्थापित नारीवादी समालोचना नितान्त नौलो पद्धति र दृष्टिकोण हो । यसले साहित्यिक कृतिहरूमा नारीसमस्याका रूपमा देखापरेका पितृसत्तात्मक व्यवस्थाका मूल्यमान्यताको प्रतिरोध र प्रतिवादका लागि सशक्त नारीचरित्र र नारीकेन्द्री चिन्तनको अपेक्षा गरेको हुन्छ । पुँजीवाद र पितृसत्ताको अन्तर्सम्बन्धमा व्यापक विमर्श चाहने नारीवादी समालोचनाको मूल आधार नारीचेतनामा एकातिर आर्थिक–सांस्कृतिक पक्षका विसङ्गतिलाई नछिमल्दासम्म नारीउत्पीडन र शोषण यथावत् रहने कुरा गरिएको छ भने अर्कातिर यसले सामाजिक विभेद, पुरुषकेन्द्री परनिर्भरता, लैङ्गिक हिंसा र परम्परित विवाहप्रथा नारीमुक्तिका बाधक हुन् भन्ने मान्यता अगाडि सारेको छ । नारीस्वतन्त्रताको वकालत गर्ने यस चेतनाका अनुयायीहरूले महिलासमस्याका बहुआयाममा ध्यान केन्द्रित गर्दै अत्याचारहीन, शोषणमुक्त र समतामूलक नारीसत्ताका लागि नारीस्रष्टा नै सक्रिय हुनुपर्ने आवाज बुलन्द गरेका छन् । नेपाली कथासाहित्यमा नारीहरूका अनेक पीडा र भोगाइलाई पुरुषसत्ताका आवरणमा प्रस्तुत गर्न मनपराउने पद्मावती सिंहको ‘‘अग्रगामी’ कथा नारीवादी चेतनालाई अभिव्यक्ति दिने सशक्त रचना भएकाले यसको अध्ययनमा नारीचेतनाका सैद्धान्तिक परिप्रेक्ष्यलाई सहयोगी बनाइएको छ । विवाहप्रथाका आडमा यथास्थितिवादी पुरुषसत्ताका कारण नारीहरूले भोगेका नारीउत्पीडन र शोषण, नारीको वैयक्तिक स्वतन्त्रता र स्वाभिमानलाई महŒव नदिने र नारीजीवनलाई मूल्यहीन ठान्ने तथा नारीअस्मिताको अवमूल्यन गर्ने पुरुषचिन्तनलाई मुख्यरूपमा विवेचनाको परिधिभित्र राखिएको छ र यस कथाकी केन्द्रीय चरित्र उर्वराका कार्यव्यापारबाट अभिव्यक्त नारीवादी चेतनाका अनेक पक्षहरूकोसाक्ष्यसहित समीक्षा गर्दै यस अध्ययनमा पाठपरक निष्कर्ष दिइएको छ ।
american_english: Feminist criticism, established in Western literary theory as an achievement of the feminist movement, is a distinctly new method and perspective. It expects strong female characters and women-centered thinking in order to resist and protest the values of the patriarchal system that appear in literary works as women's problems. While on the one hand feminist criticism, which calls for broad discussion of the interrelationship between capitalism and patriarchy, states that women's oppression and exploitation will remain unchanged as long as the incongruities in the economic and cultural aspects of women's consciousness are not brought to light, on the other hand it has put forward the view that social discrimination, male-centered dependence, gender violence, and the traditional marriage system are obstacles to women's liberation. Adherents of this consciousness, which advocates women's freedom, have raised their voices, focusing on the multiple dimensions of women's problems, that women creators themselves must become active in pursuit of a violence-free, exploitation-free, and egalitarian women's power. Because Padmavati Singh's story “Agradami” (Agradami Katha), which in Nepali story literature prefers to present the many pains and sufferings of women under the cover of male power, is a powerful work expressing feminist consciousness, the theoretical perspective of women's consciousness has been made a support in its study. The analysis primarily places within its scope the oppression and exploitation experienced by women because of status-quoist male power under the guise of the marriage system, the male thinking that does not value women's personal freedom and self-respect and considers women's lives worthless, and that devalues women's identity, and by reviewing with evidence the many aspects of feminist consciousness expressed through the actions of this story's central character, Urbara, this study presents a text-based conclusion.

informal_english: Feminist criticism, which came out of the feminist movement and took hold in Western literary theory, is a totally new method and way of looking at things. It looks for strong female characters and women-centred thinking to push back against and protest the values of the patriarchal system that show up in literary works as women's problems. On one hand, feminist criticism—which wants a wide-ranging discussion of how capitalism and patriarchy are tied together—says that women's oppression and exploitation will stay the same as long as the contradictions in the economic and cultural sides of women's consciousness aren't exposed, and on the other hand it has argued that social discrimination, male-centred dependence, gender violence, and the traditional marriage system are barriers to women's liberation. People who follow this consciousness, which stands up for women's freedom, have spoken up loud and clear, focusing on the many sides of women's problems, saying that women creators themselves need to get active in the fight for a violence-free, exploitation-free, and equal women's power. Because Padmavati Singh's story “Agradami” (Agradami Katha), which in Nepali story literature tends to present the many pains and struggles of women under the cover of male power, is a powerful piece expressing feminist consciousness, the theoretical perspective of women's consciousness has been used as a support in studying it. The analysis mainly keeps within its scope the oppression and exploitation women have faced because of status-quoist male power under the guise of the marriage system, the male mindset that doesn't value women's personal freedom and self-respect and sees women's lives as worthless, and that devalues women's identity, and by looking over, with evidence, the many sides of feminist consciousness expressed through the actions of this story's central character, Urbara, this study offers a text-based conclusion.
translator_notes: The title 'अग्रगामी कथा' is transliterated as 'Agradami' (Agradami Katha) in line with the source's parenthetical form. The character name 'उर्वरा' is rendered as 'Urbara' by transliteration. The source contains the character 'Œ' in 'महŒव', treated as 'mahattva/importance/value' in context.
